section_entries.mathematical_role: Realizes the minimum-along-an-interval covariance as Brownian diffusion on a tree and gives an explicit discrete Gaussian recursion.

unit_result_entry.title: Minimum-along-path covariance realized by a Gaussian tree
unit_result_entry.why_material: The section explains positive semidefiniteness structurally: minimum covariance is common ancestral Brownian history, and the discrete father map yields an explicit independent-increment recursion with the prescribed covariance.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Includes both the continuous Le Gall tree analogy and the finite Gaussian construction needed for the paper's covariance matrix.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Depends on formulas (4.1)-(4.3) and the ancestor/father definitions; one formula-number cross-reference appears inconsistent in extraction, but the construction and covariance claim are clear.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Critical-line prime covariance from the prime number theorem
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: At epsilon_t at most order 1/log t the abscissa shift is negligible, and Lemma 3.4 turns the prime covariance into an oscillatory integral whose cutoff relative to log t again yields c wedge 1.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The minimum-type covariance is made concrete by decomposing fluctuation into shared history plus independent increments, expressed once as Brownian/disordered components and once as diffusion or recursion on an ancestral tree.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The constructions realize the Gaussian covariance law; they do not derive the zeta theorem independently of the analytic arguments.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Covariance positivity through shared ancestry
